title: The Cost of the Holiday Behind a Corrected Declaration
content:
The cost of the holiday behind a corrected declaration on the Travel Protection Plans is read from the
operator's own record for the packaged holiday held under the Vacation Package Products, together with the
ledger of charges standing against it.

## The three readings

| What the operator's record and ledger show | The cost of the holiday |
|---|---|
| The record stands confirmed and the ledger carries a final payment | The charges standing on that ledger: the deposits taken, the final payment and the charges raised for optional components, added together |
| The record stands confirmed and the ledger carries no final payment | The money that record shows paid |
| Neither of those | The price the package was quoted at |

## Points of judgement

A holiday whose record stands quoted, cancelled or in any state other than confirmed falls to the third reading
whatever its ledger carries, and its cost is the price the package was quoted at. A confirmed holiday on which
only a deposit has been taken falls to the second reading, and its cost is the money the record shows paid,
which may be less than the price quoted. A confirmed holiday whose ledger carries a final payment falls to the
first, and its cost is the total of the charges on that ledger, which may stand above or below the price quoted
according to what optional components were added.
